title: The Integration Boost's payment address, chain and data-submitter are ratified Artifact parameters, not operational settings
content:
A.2.2.9.2.2.3.6.3 writes eight parameters from the approved proposal into the Instance Configuration Document: Integration Partner Name, Integration Partner Reward Address, Integration Partner Chain, Integration Boost Cadence, Data Submission Format, Data Submission Responsible Actor, Savings Rate Adjustment Strategy, and Custom Instance Parameters.

The **reward address** is the striking inclusion. In most systems the destination of a recurring payment is operational configuration, changeable by whoever runs payments. Here it is a governed field: it enters at planning (A.2.2.9.2.2.3.1.3), survives GovOps review, is approved in the token holder vote, and is written into the Artifact. Redirecting payments therefore requires the full Invocation-grade governance path, not an administrative edit.

The same applies to the **data submission responsible actor**. Given that the identity of the submitting party is expected to migrate over time — from the Core Council Risk Advisor to a partner, contractor, Prime Agent or GovOps (A.2.2.9.2.2.1.2.2) — pinning it in the Artifact means each such migration is a ratified change with a record, not a quiet handoff.

What this buys is that the two facts most exploitable in a payment stream — where money goes and who reports the numbers that determine how much — are both under token holder control and both publicly readable in the Agent's Artifact.
description: Partner name, reward address, chain, cadence, submission format and responsible actor are all copied from the approved proposal into the Instance Configuration Document by token holder vote.
